R101.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search(filterArgs) escapes each arg per RFC 2254/4515; explicit new SearchControls() is equivalent to the original's null (default) controls.

R102.note: path.basename() is the right restriction for a require() sink; strips traversal without rejecting plain filenames.

R103.note: Manual escaping of *, (, ), \, NUL to hex form is the standard correct mitigation for DirectorySearcher.Filter concatenation.

R104.note: archive/tar replacement closes the shell vector, but the ctx parameter is now unused so request cancellation (required by the stated contract) is silently dropped, not disclosed in the write-up.

R105.note: Eliminates process execution entirely via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping; the behavioral rewrite is stated openly and preserves the connectivity-check goal for legitimate callers.

R106.note: SecureRandom() removes the attacker-controllable seed from token generation; the write-up explicitly discloses that seed no longer affects the output.

R107.note: Idiomatic @Lazy self-injection routes deleteInvoice() through the AOP proxy so @PreAuthorize is enforced; no other observable change.

R108.note: Express sendFile's root option is the canonical fix for this sink and blocks no legitimate single-file download.

R109.note: execFile('whois', [domain]) spawns the real whois binary directly (no shell reparsing), verified against Node v24 to not invoke a shell; closes the reported shell-injection vector.

R110.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the correct root-cause fix, activating the @PreAuthorize checks already declared in the service as intended.

R111.note: Narrowing supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken is the framework-idiomatic fix for an overly broad AuthenticationProvider match; other providers/tokens unaffected.

R112.note: Reproduced against real powershell.exe: tokens after '-Command "..."' are not bound to $args (Count stays 0) - injected text after -ArgumentList still executes as script (confirmed 'Write-Output INJECTED' ran), so the vector is not closed, and the real serverName never reaches Test-Connection, silently breaking the endpoint for all legitimate input.

R113.note: Reproduced against Node v24 execFile('cmd.exe', ['/c', scriptPath, reportName]) on Windows: an embedded double-quote in reportName breaks Node's cmd.exe argument quoting and executes injected commands (confirmed whoami ran), so the reported vector remains exploitable despite using execFile with an array.

R114.note: Deny-by-default JexlSandbox with newInstance(false) is an appropriate constrained-evaluator replacement for arbitrary GroovyShell.evaluate(); the narrowed formula surface matches the documented arithmetic/comparison use case, not an arbitrary added restriction.

R115.note: java.nio.file listing correctly removes Runtime.exec(), but adds a new rejection of absolute paths and '..' that the original code did not enforce; disclosed in the write-up, so it is a stated restriction rather than a silent one.
